subject: part
title: PART.-----ALT.F.
description: Second diagram on page 437 (MP(I)-11). The crossing diagrams how participation structurally meets alternative-functionalism: PART (participation, again on the subject axis with the arrow — on the right this time) crossed with ALT-F (alternative functionalism — the form's actual alternative-working). PART sits at the right with the subject-arrow; ACT (action) sits at the upper-right and OMT-DY (omitted dynamics) hangs to its right as the subject-side rightward outputs. TRS (transformation) sits centrally below as the subject's downward output. POL-CON (political consideration) anchors the upper-left and IST-ACT (isolated-source activism) sits at the left margin as partner-side upper outputs. ALT-F sits at center-left as partner-axis; SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) hangs at the lower-left as partner-side downward output. LK-IMP (linkage implication) sits centrally as the bridging hub, with CULT-TF-S (cultural-transfer source) at lower-center, (R)INTR (the reality of introduction) below CULT-TF-S, and OBS (observation) at the bottom as the bridging-axis downward terminus. Structural argument: when participation is crossed with alternative-functionalism, the upper diagonal from PART out to ACT routes participation into action, but the action chain produces OMT-DY — omitted-dynamics — meaning what's *missing* from the participation's working when only action is its partner-side route. The partner's upper chain POL-CON → IST-ACT → ALT-F routes political-consideration through isolated-source activism into alternative-functionalism — but ALT-F then routes only to SOC-RT-DY on the lower-left, producing social-reality-dynamics on the partner-side alone. The central bridging chain LK-IMP → CULT-TF-S → (R)INTR → OBS is the *full route*: linkage-implication routes through cultural-transfer-source into the reality of introduction and finally into observation. This is the structural path the prose needs the activist to hold — LK-IMP must hold all four edges for participation to actually reach alternative-functionalism without being stranded as either OMT-DY on the subject-side or SOC-RT-DY alone on the partner-side.
